item.title: Coptic iconoclasm
item.description:
Source: TW

Cyril

The political influence of Coptic Christians has declined significantly. Coptic bishops like Cyril of Alexandria once commanded their own private paramilitaries (parabalani) which would intimidate opponents, riot in the streets, etc. in order to enforce the bishop’s will. Their reputation for violence was so notorious that the Roman Emperors in Constantinople tried to curb their power by reducing their numbers, stripping the bishop of direct control over them, and placing them under the authority of the secular governor.
